rushing_yards.mechanism: Rushing yards = rush attempts x yards per attempt. Attempts come from team rush volume (neutral run rate, script: favorites and leading teams run more, trailing teams less) times the player's carry share in the committee; yards per attempt from OL run blocking and yards before contact, RB creation (yards over expected), opponent front and box counts and a heavy explosive-run tail. Variance is high because a few long runs dominate.
rushing_yards.target: Probability a player's rushing yards (or attempts) exceed a threshold, or exceed another player.

inputs.why: Production and historical voting model.
Voters reward team success, so award probability depends on team win and seed distributions.
Electorate composition, ballot close date and tie rules determine which information can still affect the result.
Narrative momentum, injuries and highlight events shift media odds and voters' perception.
Availability for remaining games.
Efficiency-based performance baseline for QB candidates, who win most MVP votes.
TD hot streaks inflate narratives; regression suggests production may be overstated.
Accrual and remaining schedule.
Remaining opponent difficulty.
The price path reveals narrative momentum and how the market reacts to each week's performances.
Sportsbook and media award odds provide the benchmark for pricing the candidate set.
Eligibility (e.g. rookie status), definition of the award and which body announces determine the candidate set.

interactions.hypothesis: Team record x production: voters give a premium to candidates on top-seeded teams, so the same stat line has different win probability across team records.
Late-season injury x ballot timing: an injury after ballots close doesn't reduce vote share, but one before reduces; the timing of voting matters.
TD luck x narrative: high-TD stretches raise media odds temporarily; regress TD luck to estimate true production.

season_awards.label: Season awards (MVP, OPOY, DPOY, ROY and similar)
season_awards.mechanism: Winner probability = P(candidate survives injuries and team results) x P(voters choose him | stats, team success, narrative). Production features (EPA, yards, TDs vs peers), team record and positional bias determine the candidate set; the narrative path through the season and ballot timing determines the vote; injuries and team collapse eliminate candidates. Markets are generally anchored to media/sportsbook odds.
season_awards.target: Which candidate is named winner of an annual award by the official body.

inputs.why: Realized totals plus projected remainder is the structure of any in-season probability.
Missed games are the principal tail risk for season-long counting stats and leaders.
Leader contracts resolve as a maximum over many correlated players, needing simulation of the whole field.
Target volume projects receiving yards, receptions and receiving TDs.
Carry share and goal-line usage project rushing yards and TDs.
QB efficiency prior converts projected attempts into yards and TDs.
Fantasy contracts are linear combinations of components whose covariances matter for rank outcomes.
TD totals regress strongly; used to adjust projection of both realized and expected TDs.
Remaining defenses by position adjust the projected per-game rate.
Teammate changes and injuries during the season shift usage and leader probability.
Per-game variance aggregates across games and sets the spread of season totals.
Team volume tendencies project season-long attempts and thus counting stats.
Contract defines eligible games (regular season only), the stat source and tiebreak rules for leaders.

interactions.hypothesis: Games-played attrition x per-game rate: high-rate injury-prone players have lower leader probability than rate-only models suggest.
TD regression x accrued total: regress TD rate on remaining games.
Remaining schedule x role: soft remaining defenses lift receivers only when target share is stable.

season_player_stats_and_leaders.label: Season player stats, leaders, weekly leaders and fantasy
season_player_stats_and_leaders.mechanism: Season stat = sum of per-game outputs over games played; project per-game rate from role, team volume and efficiency with regression, multiply by games-played distribution, add realized to date, and simulate. Leader markets are order statistics over correlated contenders, weekly leaders have much higher randomness. Rule wording determines eligible games (regular season only) and stat source.
season_player_stats_and_leaders.target: Probability a player or team reaches a season (or weekly) statistical threshold, leads the league, or outranks another in a stat.

inputs.why: The simulation turns team ratings and schedules into correlated win, seed and title probabilities with proper tiebreakers.
Time-varying rating with uncertainty.
Preseason ratings need regression based on how much of last year's production returns, especially at QB and lines.
Forward-looking opponent strength changes expected wins; stale last-year records mislead.
Records overstated by close-game luck should be regressed before using them for future win expectations.
Takeaway luck inflates records and ratings; using expected turnovers gives a truer strength estimate.
QB injury and quality dominate team win variance, and replacement QB scenarios matter for season simulations.
Distribution of key-player absences (QB, EDGE, OL) widens win distributions and lowers the title odds of top-heavy teams.
Current injuries and expected return dates adjust near-term ratings and in-season futures.
Title and conference markets depend on seed, bye and bracket path, not only team rating.
Late-season rest and incentives.
Bye placement and rest differences in the schedule shift expected wins marginally across teams.
Linked futures must satisfy sum-to-one and implication constraints; violations flag stale or mispriced contracts.
Sportsbook futures prices provide the benchmark probabilities after de-vig, although they are vig-heavy.
Price drift around injuries and results shows how quickly futures incorporate new information.
Ties, cancelled/forfeited games.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.

interactions.hypothesis: QB risk x schedule: probability the QB misses games and which opponents those games are against changes the win distribution non-linearly.
Close-game luck x rating: teams outperforming Pythagorean expectation carry inflated ratings and regress in the second half; the simulation should use luck-adjusted ratings.
Seed x bracket path: bye and home field make title odds convex in seeding probability.
Market coherence x liquidity: where linked futures violate sum-to-one, the least liquid contract is likely stale.

season_win_totals_and_futures.label: Season win totals, playoffs, division, conference and Super Bowl futures
season_win_totals_and_futures.mechanism: Simulate the remaining season from time-varying team strength with uncertainty, QB and key-player availability, home/rest effects and the full tiebreaker rules; produce correlated probabilities for wins, playoffs, seeds, division, conference and championship. Preseason rating priors blend last-year ratings with roster continuity regression and market win totals; in-season updates use adjusted efficiency and luck regression. Cross-market coherence (sum-to-one, implications) constrains the family set and exposes stale quotes.
season_win_totals_and_futures.target: Probability of season-long team outcomes: win count thresholds or exact wins, playoffs, division, seed, conference title, Super Bowl, head-to-head season comparisons.

inputs.why: Implied team means from game spread/total.
The team's own opponent-adjusted offense determines its points per drive independent of the other side.
Opponent defense efficiency (pass vs rush).
Own plays and drives, which depend on both offense tempo and the opponent's clock-usage, set the possessions for team points.
Possessions allocated to team.
Team-specific red-zone TD conversion sets points per trip; shrunk to league average.
Own kicker accuracy and range add FG points when drives stall, and affect clusters at multiples of 3.
The team's starting QB status is the dominant driver of its own total and resolves late.
Own OL health shifts sack/pressure rates and run efficiency, affecting points per drive.
Absence of receivers and backs reduces the team's scoring ceiling.
Field position and opponent turnovers.
Weather effects scaled by style.
Lead/trail effect on the team's late scoring.
Team-score mass at multiples of 3/7.
Sportsbook team totals and implied splits from spread and total give the benchmark for team-total rungs.
Consistency with game total and spread.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread-implied split x blowout script: a heavy favorite's team total has a right tail from long drives but a left tail from clock-killing late; the underdog gains garbage points.
Opponent pass-defense x team pass rate: a pass-heavy offense is hurt more by a strong pass defense; run-heavy offense by run defense.
QB injury x OL: a backup QB behind a weak OL reduces points more than QB value alone.

team_total.label: Team total points
team_total.mechanism: Team points = team possessions x points per possession, bounded by the game total and spread split (mu = (T +/- s)/2). The relevant inputs are the team's own offense efficiency against the opponent's defense, pace and clock control (possessions), red-zone and kicker finishing, QB/OL/skill availability and weather; distribution is right-skewed with discrete clusters at multiples of 3 and 7. Team-total rungs must be consistent with game total and spread quotes.
team_total.target: Probability one team's points exceed a rung in the game, per wording on overtime.

inputs.why: Correlation structure between legs determines joint probability.
Team strength underlies winner/margin legs.
Team total consistency across legs.
Script links spreads, totals and player props.
Key-number lattice for margin legs.
Marginal distribution for player legs.
Combo price versus correlated product.
Per-leg void and push handling.
Fees scale with price and apply to the combo as a whole, so a thin correlation edge can be consumed by fee plus spread on the combined contract.
Combo books thinner; slippage large.

interactions.hypothesis: Winner and total legs interact via scoring script: a favorite winning correlates with the over only when its offense drives the margin, not when it wins through defense.
QB yardage and team total legs are positively correlated via pass volume, but negatively correlated with the favorite covering in garbage time.
Per-leg wording interacts with fees: voided legs change the effective payout and combo pricing, so compare executable price after fees to joint probability.

combo.mechanism: Combo and parlay markets multiply legs whose outcomes are correlated through game script, team strength and shared stat sources; a fair price requires the joint probability, not the product. Contract wording per leg (void/push handling, overtime) and fees affect value, and executable liquidity is thinner.
combo.target: Joint probability that all (or specified) legs resolve as required, under each leg's wording and the combo's own voiding rules.

inputs.why: Who receives first shifts first-score probability by several percentage points.
Opening-drive scripts give team-specific first-drive scoring rates.
Efficiency determines hazard of scoring on each possession.
Opposing defense efficiency suppresses hazard.
Faster tempo increases number of plays before a reference time.
Red-zone finish determines TD vs FG for first score type.
FG range and accuracy matter for first-score timing when drives stall.
Expected scoring split by team gives baseline hazards.
Early turnovers create short fields and quick scores.
What counts as scoring (TD, FG, safety) and how ties/no-score resolve.

interactions.hypothesis: Receiving first and scripted opening drive: a team with high opening-drive TD rate and the first possession is much more likely to score first than the average, and the opposite for slow starters.
Kicker range and weather change whether first-score hazard is TD or FG, shifting timing distribution for TD-specific markets.
Pace affects the number of plays available before a time threshold, so high tempo teams have higher early scoring hazard.

first_event.mechanism: First-score and race-to-N markets resolve on the earliest scoring events: opening possession, scripted early plays, red-zone and kicker behaviour, turnovers giving short fields, and overall team scoring rates. The probability that a team scores first is roughly proportional to its share of early scoring hazard, shifted by who has the ball first; timing markets integrate the hazard over play time.
first_event.target: Which team scores first (or reaches N points first) and at what game time, under contract definition of scoring play.

inputs.why: Margin distribution mass near zero determines overtime probability and tie mass.
OT rules and rate underpin OT-related events.
Event counts scale with plays and drives.
Turnover and takeaway hazards drive event counts such as turnovers or defensive TDs.
Pass-rush strength drives sacks and safeties.
Weak pass blocking raises sack and safety hazard.
Red-zone finishing governs TD counts.
Rare-event base rates conditioned on style.
Penalty-heavy games alter drive counts.
Weather shifts pass rate and thus sacks, turnovers and scoring events.
Expected team scoring is the basis for count markets.
Event definitions (OT inclusion, which team, official scoring) must be matched.

interactions.hypothesis: Close pre-game spread interacts with total to determine overtime probability: tight, low-scoring games with kicker-dependent scoring have more mass on ties.
Pass-rush strength interacts with OL weakness and QB time-to-throw to raise sack, safety and turnover hazards.
Turnover luck interacts with scoring: takeaways produce short fields and drive TD counts, so realized turnover luck should be regressed before using it for event hazards.

game_event.mechanism: Game-event and stat markets (overtime, safety, both teams score, team stats, TD counts, period TDs) are tails or slices of the underlying drive and score process. They depend on base rates of rare events (overtime, safeties, defensive TDs), the correlation structure of scoring, and team style indicators (pass rush, red-zone play, turnovers) that shift event hazards.
game_event.target: Occurrence or count of a game-level event or team stat (overtime, safety, touchdowns, turnovers, sacks, etc.) under the contract definition.

inputs.why: Market-implied and Elo-style team strength is the prior that every other input must add to.
Starter QB status is the largest single swing in margin and resolves late; must be mixed by probability.
Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency gives the structural mean margin independent of the line.
Defense efficiency completes the team-strength matchup; pass and rush splits matter for specific opponents.
Timestamped injury vintages show which stars are missing at market time.
Short weeks, byes and travel create small systematic margin shifts.
Home-field strength, roof and surface adjust the margin mean.
Wind/precipitation compress scoring and favor the run-heavy/defense-heavy side.
Key-number lattice converts rating differences to probabilities at half-point spreads.
Tie/OT mass differs between regulation-only and including-OT settlement.
Seeding stakes and starter rest change effort and lineup late in the season.
Sharp reference lines are the benchmark; inconsistent Kalshi prices reveal staleness.
Settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement) must match the modelled outcome.
Division games are scouted more heavily; a candidate residual adjustment to margin variance and cover rates.
Defensive injuries alter the defense rating and are knowable from the report vintage.

interactions.hypothesis: QB-status uncertainty interacts with spread size: a backup QB shifts the margin mean and widens the margin SD, so cover probability changes more than moneyline for large spreads.
Wind and cold interact with passing-reliant teams: bad weather lowers the efficiency of pass-first favorites more than run-first teams, narrowing expected margin.
Late-season seeding stakes interact with injury reports: a clinched team with questionable starters has much higher rest probability.

game_side.mechanism: Moneyline, spread, win-margin and half/period winner markets all price the distribution of final margin: team strength differences (QB-adjusted), home edge, rest and environment shift the mean, while the lattice of NFL scoring (key numbers 3 and 7) and overtime/tie rules shape probabilities at specific lines. The market line already contains most public information, so the model is mainly a calibration and lineup-timing exercise.
game_side.target: Probability that the team wins (moneyline), covers a spread, or the margin falls in a bucket, under the contract's regulation/overtime settlement.

inputs.why: Plays per game scale all scoring; pace is a stable team trait.
Expected possessions are the base unit of scoring; drive count differs from plays due to turnovers, punts and clock-killing.
Pass-heavy teams stop the clock and sustain pace; PROE sets passing volume and yards.
Offensive EPA per play, opponent-adjusted, anchors points per drive for each team.
Opponent defense efficiency suppresses points per drive and changes the pass/rush split of scoring.
Explosive-play rates raise scoring variance and the fat right tail of the total distribution.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring opportunity by up to 4 points per trip and regresses to league mean.
Wind and precipitation lower totals; effects nonlinear.
Kicker range and accuracy determine how many stalled drives convert to 3 points and the key-number structure of totals.
Starter versus backup QB shifts both team points and pace and is only resolved late; total must be a mixture.
Teams scoring above or below their drive-efficiency expectation regress; recent points should be discounted accordingly.
Empirical total residuals and key numbers calibrate rung probabilities.
OT adds points in tied games; inclusion depends on wording.
Sharp totals incorporate weather and lineup information; the Kalshi ladder should be compared to the de-vigged consensus.

interactions.hypothesis: Pace and efficiency are multiplicative: a high-pace offense against a high-pace defense compounds possessions, while two slow, run-heavy teams under-shoot even if efficiency is average.
Wind interacts with explosive passing and kicking: high wind removes deep-pass explosives and long FG, cutting points more for vertical offenses than for run-heavy teams.
Spread size interacts with total: lopsided expected games shift clock-killing run rate for the leader, reducing the favorite's late scoring.

game_total.mechanism: Totals are the product of possessions and points per possession for both teams. Drives depend on pace, run/pass mix and turnover rates; points per drive on opponent-adjusted efficiency, field position, red-zone finishing, kicker range and weather. Both teams' outputs are correlated through game script and environment, so the distribution of total has a fat right tail from blowouts and explosive plays; both-teams-score and team-total markets are slices of the same joint distribution.
game_total.target: Sum of the two teams' points (or each team's points, or whether each team scores at least N) under the contract's regulation/OT settlement.

inputs.why: Timestamped practice status and designation are primary signals.
Inactive list is the definitive pre-game signal.
Starter ordering and role changes.
Beat reporting and coach statements often precede official reports.
Return-from-injury snap limits affect snap-threshold events.
Clinched or eliminated teams rest or limit starters in late-season games, raising the chance a player on the report is Out.
Recent snap share sets role baseline.
Coach history on resting players and use of designations.
Mid-game exit risk affects threshold events.
Market closing relative to report timing defines information set.
Definitions of active, started, played and source determine settlement.

interactions.hypothesis: Practice sequence and designation interact with position: a limited Friday practice with Questionable label implies different play probabilities for QB, RB and OL.
Seeding stakes interact with injury designation: a minor injury plus clinched seed greatly increases rest probability.
Market close time interacts with report timing: before inactives the market must hedge, after inactives it should converge to 0/1.

lineup_role.mechanism: Availability and role-event markets resolve on whether a player is active, starts, plays a threshold of snaps or has a specified role; the information chain is practice participation, official designation, coach statements, depth chart and inactive list, each arriving at known times. Probabilities come from calibrating these signals against historical outcomes by position and injury type.
lineup_role.target: Whether a player plays/starts/reaches a role threshold (active status, snap count, starter) as defined by the contract and source.

inputs.why: Timestamped reporting and source credibility.
Cap and contract timelines make events forced or unlikely.
Draft markets resolve on pick order and selections, so consensus rankings, team needs and order after trades are the baseline.
Coach hazard from record versus expectation.
Base rates for novelty events.
Team results drive firing and draft position.
Official calendars for announcements.
Resolution source and wording.
Off-field markets close at announcements or deadlines; knowing when the market closes relative to the information event avoids look-ahead.
Price reaction to leaks and reports shows how quickly insider information is absorbed and when the market is stale.

interactions.hypothesis: Reporter credibility interacts with timing: leaks close to a deadline are more informative than early speculation, and consensus across independent insiders raises confidence.
Team performance interacts with ownership signals: coach firing hazard rises with losing versus expectation, but strongly depends on contract and cap.

off_field.mechanism: Off-field markets (draft, coaching changes, transactions, Super Bowl events, weekly events) are resolved by organizational decisions, reporting and official announcements rather than play outcomes. Edge comes from institutional calendars and constraints (cap, contracts, draft order), credible reporting, base rates and precise resolution wording.
off_field.target: Occurrence or outcome of an off-field event (draft pick, coach hire/fire, transaction, event prop) as announced by the official source.

inputs.why: Team-specific historical quarter/half scoring shares are the base for period totals and margins.
Scripted first drives drive Q1 scoring and the tied-after-Q1 outcome.
Possession order shifts first-quarter and second-half-start scoring.
Two-minute drills produce a disproportionate share of Q2 points.
Lead/trail scripting determines Q3-Q4 pace and how early garbage time begins.
Full-game team strength sets the period margin mean.
Implied team totals from the game total and spread are scaled to the period.
Coaching tendencies (tempo, 4th-down aggression, halftime adjustments) vary the period profile.
Key-number structure for short periods differs from full-game residuals.
Period markets can differ on ties and overtime inclusion.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession and opening-drive scripts interact: a team that defers but has a strong scripted offense gets the ball second in Q1 yet first in Q3, shifting scoring between quarters.
Two-minute efficiency interacts with timeout and pace habits to concentrate first-half scoring in the last 2 minutes of Q2.
Halftime lead interacts with script: second-half pace and run rate depend on whether a team is leading by more than a score.

period.mechanism: Half and quarter markets inherit the full-game strength model but add period-specific structure: scripted opening drives, who receives the opening kickoff, two-minute drills before halftime, second-half adjustments and garbage-time. Scoring is smaller and lumpier per period so ties/pushes and key numbers have greater weight; late-game clock management mostly affects only the fourth quarter.
period.target: Points, margin, winner or total in a defined period (first half, quarter), settled per contract wording on ties and overtime.

inputs.why: Team pass volume is the base for QB and receiver counting stats.
Plays per game scales opportunity.
Expected game script splits volume between passing and rushing.
Target share and depth determine receiving distributions.
Carry share determines rushing volume.
Quarterback efficiency drives passing and receiver output.
Opponent adjusted position defense.
Coverage shells shape which receivers get targets.
Pressure and time to throw modify passing efficiency.
Wind and rain reduce passing and shift to rushing.
Teammate injuries redistribute volume.
Distribution shape determines ladder probabilities.
Rung consistency and implied distribution.
DNP/void rules and stat source.
Thresholds within a yard or a reception of the line are exposed to post-game stat revisions and source differences.
Realized hit rates by rung calibrate the model and expose systematic over/under-pricing of specific thresholds.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread and pass rate over expected: trailing teams throw more, so for the underdog's QB and WRs volume rises while efficiency falls against softer coverage; favorites run more.
Pressure and time to throw: a quick-release QB behind a poor OL has a low sack and efficiency loss; a slow-release QB suffers more.
Wind and deep passing: high wind cuts air yards and deep completions, hitting deep-threat receivers and QB yardage more than underneath roles.

player_other.mechanism: Player stat markets (yards, receptions, TDs, passing, rushing) are volume times efficiency, where volume comes from team plays, pass/run mix (script) and role share, and efficiency from opponent-adjusted skill, scheme and environment. Ladders over multiple thresholds require a full distribution with variance from role, script, weather and injury exit, and neighbouring rungs are strongly correlated.
player_other.target: Probability that a player's stat (passing/rushing/receiving yards, receptions, completions, TDs) exceeds a threshold (or beats another player), under official stat settlement.

inputs.why: Role-based scoring rate is the core of the player probability.
Red-zone and goal-line shares reveal opportunity concentration.
Team TD expectation sets total scoring pool.
First-drive usage sets first TD probability.
Possession order affects first scoring team.
Goal-line carry share determines rushing TD probability.
End-zone and red-zone targets determine receiving TD probability.
Injuries change shares of teammates.
Realized TD rate regresses; use opportunity not outcomes.
Opposing red-zone defense and position funneling modulate scoring.
Early exit lowers TD probability and shifts volume to others.
Whether defensive/special-teams TDs and 2-pt plays count.

interactions.hypothesis: Team total and personnel share interact: a goal-line back's TD probability rises with team rushing TD expectation but falls if the QB or WR is the preferred red-zone option, so shares must be conditional on formation.
Spread and script interact with goal-line role: trailing teams pass more near the goal line, shifting TD probability from RBs to WR/TE.
Injury to a teammate interacts with target competition to redistribute red-zone looks.

player_td.mechanism: Touchdown scorer markets (first, next, anytime) decompose into team TD expectation, player share of scoring opportunities (goal-line carries, red-zone targets, QB sneaks), timing of the first score, and opposing red-zone defense. Because scoring is rare per player and highly role-concentrated, opportunity usage beats realized TD history, and TD luck regresses.
player_td.target: Probability that a named player scores the first/next TD (or any TD) in the game under contract wording on which scores count.

inputs.why: Production features and historical voting model.
Team success strongly affects voting.
Electorate, ballot close and rules.
Narrative and injury news shift candidacy.
Candidate availability for remaining games.
Efficiency baseline for QB candidates.
TD hot streaks overstate candidacy.
Market price path indicates narrative momentum.
Award definition and eligibility.
Sportsbook award odds as benchmark.

interactions.hypothesis: Team record interacts with production: voters reward high production on winning teams, so a candidate's probability depends on joint standings and statistical rank.
Ballot timing interacts with injuries and late news: if ballots close before the playoffs, late-season injuries still count in the regular-season vote but later narratives do not.

season_award.mechanism: Season awards depend on production relative to peers, team success, narrative momentum and voting mechanics (electorate, ballot timing, position bias). Statistical standing predicts the candidate set but the winner emerges from voter behavior; late-season performance and visible highlights shift media odds, and injury or team collapse can end a candidacy.
season_award.target: Which player wins an annual award (MVP, OPOY, DPOY, ROY, etc.) as announced by the official body.

inputs.why: Monte Carlo of the schedule with tiebreakers.
Time-varying team strength with uncertainty.
Preseason regression and offseason changes.
Forward-looking schedule difficulty.
Close-game luck regresses; avoids overreaction to records.
QB injury risk and replacement quality dominate season variance.
Season win and playoff odds depend on how many games key players (QB especially) miss, and the distribution of absences is skewed.
Seed and bye effects on title odds.
Constraints across linked markets.
Late-season incentives and rest.
Sportsbook futures prices as benchmark.
Ties, forfeits and cancelled-game handling.

interactions.hypothesis: QB availability interacts with schedule: a backup QB in games against strong divisional opponents changes the win-count distribution non-linearly and the tiebreaker path.
Close-game luck and Pythagorean records interact with the market win total: teams outperforming expected wins have inflated implied ratings and regress.
Bracket path interacts with seed: the one seed bye and home field boost title odds more than the rating difference alone implies.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-level outcome markets (win totals, division, conference, Super Bowl, playoffs, seeds, head-to-head) derive from team strength with uncertainty, schedule, injuries (especially QB) and tiebreaker/bracket rules; simulation produces a coherent set of probabilities in which markets are linked by constraints. Preseason priors rely on roster continuity and regression of past results, in-season updates shift via ratings and luck-adjusted records.
season_outcome.target: Probability of season-long team outcomes (win count, playoff/seed/division/conference/SB result, head-to-head season comparisons) under the contract definition.

inputs.why: Realized accrual plus projected remainder.
Games-played risk from injuries.
Max-of-N modeling for leader markets.
Target volume per game is the base for receiving yards, receptions and TD leaders; it must be projected with role stability in mind.
Carry share and goal-line role project season rushing yards and TDs; committee changes mid-season are the main risk.
A regressed QB efficiency prior converts projected attempts to season passing yards and TDs, avoiding overreaction to early-season hot or cold stretches.
Bottom-up fantasy points translation.
Remaining opponents, adjusted by position-specific defense, change per-game expectation and are partly knowable from the schedule.
Season TD totals are the noisiest component; regressing TD luck lowers exceedance probabilities for players who are ahead of pace and raises them for those behind.
Injuries and roster changes to teammates reallocate volume mid-season, so the leader probability moves with the supporting cast.
Game-level variance for aggregation.
Definition of eligible games, ties, and stat source.

interactions.hypothesis: Games-played attrition interacts with per-game rate: leader probabilities for high-rate but injury-prone players are lower than a rate-only model suggests.
Remaining schedule interacts with role stability: soft remaining defenses lift receivers more if target share is stable.
TD regression interacts with realized accrual: players with TD luck to date should have their remaining-season TD rate regressed, lowering exceedance probabilities.

season_stat.mechanism: Season-long statistical markets (leaders, totals, fantasy, team events, weekly leaders) are sums of per-game outputs integrated over games played, role changes and schedule, and for leader markets an order statistic over many correlated contenders. Early in the season priors dominate; as games accumulate realized totals plus remaining expectation drive probability.
season_stat.target: Season or weekly statistical outcome (player total over threshold, league leader, fantasy rank, team event count) under contract definition.

m.combo_pricing.label: Combo/parlay price versus correlated-leg product
m.combo_pricing.measurement: Compute joint probability by simulation with game-level correlation (nfl.corr), compare with executable combo price after fees; verify settlement wording for each leg and void/push handling.
m.combo_pricing.mechanism: A combo's fair price equals the joint probability of legs; naive product of marginals ignores correlation, so a quoted combo price relative to joint model estimate reveals mispricing.
m.combo_pricing.rationale: Combos amplify errors: positively correlated legs (team win and over) are worth more than the product; negatively correlated worth less; also fees and liquidity are larger for combos.

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook and exchange reference prices with timestamps

nfl.td_luck.label: Touchdown luck and yards-to-points regression
nfl.td_luck.measurement: TD over expected = actual TDs minus expected TDs from carry/target location (yard line, game state), using expected points/TD models (ff_opportunity expected TD fields). Shrink luck to zero (e.g. 70-85% regression) and keep a smaller persistent player/role residual estimated across seasons.
nfl.td_luck.mechanism: Touchdowns per yard or per target for a player or team above/below the expected rate given field position and usage are largely noise, producing regression in subsequent games and in season totals.
nfl.td_luck.rationale: TD props and totals are repriced on a recent hot streak; the true expectation depends on opportunity (red-zone touches, targets inside the 10) not on realized TDs. Subtle: some players (large TE/QB sneakers) have persistently higher TD rates than yardage implies.

nfl.td_rates.label: Anytime and first-TD scoring rates by role
nfl.td_rates.measurement: Expected team touchdowns = (team total - FG expectation)/7 approximately; allocate by player share of expected TDs (red-zone/goal-line role and receiving usage), calibrate shares with shrinkage; first-TD = P(team first) x player share of that team's first TDs.
nfl.td_rates.mechanism: Per-game probability of scoring is a function of expected team TDs, the player's share of scoring opportunities, and the correlation of scoring across teammates; first-TD adds a timing component.
nfl.td_rates.rationale: Anytime TD probability should be built from a team TD expectation and player share (Poisson/multinomial) rather than a flat historical rate; first-TD markets additionally weigh which team scores first and the player share of first-possession usage.

nfl.team_total_split.label: Team-points share model (implied total and spread to team means)
nfl.team_total_split.measurement: Compute implied team means from the closing spread and total (mu_A = (T - s)/2 etc.), adjust for team-specific scoring variance and key-number structure; compare team total quotes to the implied pair to detect inconsistent pricing.
nfl.team_total_split.mechanism: The game total and spread jointly imply each team's expected points: team A = (total + spread-to-A)/2; team totals markets depend on this split and on variance of each team separately.
nfl.team_total_split.rationale: Team total and combined markets must be consistent with the game market; the split depends on spread and total only if the market is efficient; deviations signal mispricing; allowing for scoring styles (high-variance team) matters.

nfl.turnovers.label: Turnover rate and takeaway luck regression
nfl.turnovers.measurement: Offensive giveaways per play (INT rate with QB prior, fumble rate) and defensive takeaways per play; decompose INT into turnover-worthy/pressure/deflection and fumbles into forced vs recovered; regress recovered-fumble share to 50%; use opponent-adjusted rates with long half-life. Compare realized to expected from pressure and QB aggressiveness.
nfl.turnovers.mechanism: Turnovers swing possession counts and field position; offensive giveaway rates are mostly QB-driven and persistent in part, while defensive takeaways (especially fumble recoveries and INTs) regress heavily.
nfl.turnovers.rationale: Forecasting should use expected turnovers from process (pressure, tipped balls, aggressive throws, ball security) rather than realized takeaways; realized takeaway differential is a notorious regressor that markets sometimes overreact to.

nfl.weather_pit.measurement: Store forecasts (wind speed/gust, temperature, precipitation probability) at fixed lead times before kickoff for open-air stadiums; map to stadium coordinates and kickoff hour; ignore for domes; compute wind component along field (cross vs head); calibrate effect on totals, pass rate and FG make rates.
nfl.weather_pit.mechanism: Wind, rain, snow and cold reduce passing efficiency, deep passing, kicking accuracy and scoring, and raise run share; forecasts update through game week.
nfl.weather_pit.rationale: Weather effects are non-linear: wind above ~15 mph sharply cuts deep-ball and FG efficiency, while temperature has small effects unless extreme; roofs neutralize them. Using realized weather leaks information; forecast vintages at market time are required.
